quiz_item.question: Before mixing two-part epoxy or polyester resin with fiberglass or carbon fiber reinforcement for Composite Materials Requirement 1, what safety precautions are mandatory?
options: A. Mix large batches of resin and catalyst in a tall, narrow plastic cup inside an unventilated closet and handle cut glass fibers with bare hands.

B. Read the Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all resins and hardeners, work in a well-ventilated area, wear chemical-resistant nitrile gloves, safety goggles, long sleeves, and an appropriate dust mask/respirator, and mix small batches in shallow containers to prevent runaway exothermic heat.
C. Heat the hardener catalyst over an open flame to speed up curing and blow fiberglass sanding dust across the room with compressed air.
D. Wash uncured epoxy resin off bare skin using acetone or lacquer thinner so the solvent carries the chemicals deeper into your pores.

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Composite Materials to Complete Two): Step 1 (Use composite materials to complete): When you saturate the fiberglass reinforcement with resin, air can be trapped in the laminate, creating voids (p. 60).

Step 3 (Composite Materials to Complete Two): Step 3 (Use composite materials to complete): To remove air bubbles, use a squeegee or a paint roller to push the saturated glass reinforcement evenly down to the mold surface, squeezing air (p. 60).

pamphlet_excerpts: Careers & Professional Pathways: Careers in the Composites Industry The composites industry offers many career opportunities (p. 72).

Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 2: You might find a position with a company that produces the raw materials used in manufacturing composites, or a company that makes composite parts (p. 72).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 3: You might work at a university or in a laboratory doing research and development on new materials or processes (p. 72).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 4: You might work in design, creating new applications for composite materials (p. 72).

options: A. Mix large batches of resin and catalyst in a tall, narrow plastic cup inside an unventilated closet and handle cut glass fibers with bare hands.

C. Heat the hardener catalyst over an open flame to speed up curing and blow fiberglass sanding dust across the room with compressed air.
D. Wash uncured epoxy resin off bare skin using acetone or lacquer thinner so the solvent carries the chemicals deeper into your pores.
